source_refs.note: Book p. 52-53: 2.10.2 definition, global extrema, Example (a)-(c) with Figures 2.2-2.4, local maxima/minima table, Figure 2.5

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein sab se bari value (global maximum) dekhi thi. Ab us ka ulta: sab se chhoti value, yani global (absolute) minimum. Phir hum ek nayi aur bohat ahem cheez seekhenge: local (relative) maxima aur minima, jo poore interval ke bajaye sirf aas paas ke points se muqabla karte hain. Yeh sabaq is section ka dil hai, is liye figures ko ghor se dekhiye.

Kitab ki definition: maan lijiye \(I\) ek interval hai aur \(f: I \to \mathbb{R}\) ek function hai. Hum kehte hain ke \(f\) ka \(x = c \in I\) par global (absolute) minimum hai, agar \(I\) ke har \(x\) ke liye \(f(c) \le f(x)\).
Agar \(f(x)\) ka \(x = c\) par global (absolute) minimum ho, to \(f(c)\) ko function ki global (absolute) minimum value kehte hain.
Function ke global maximum aur global minimum ko mila kar us ke global extrema kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh 2.10.1 wali definition hi hai, bas inequality ulti ho gayi: ab \(f(c)\) kisi bhi doosri value se bara nahin hota. "Extrema" lafz "extremum" ki jama (plural) hai; is mein maxima aur minima dono aate hain. Jaise class ka sab se kam number bhi ek "extreme" hai aur sab se zyada bhi.

blocks.title: Example (a)
blocks.problem: Let \(f(x) = x^{2}\) be defined on the interval \([0, 2]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{2}\), interval \([0, 2]\) par.
Maloom karna: global maximum aur global minimum.
Tareeqa: \([0, 2]\) par \(f'(x) = 2x \ge 0\), yani \(f\) yahan increasing hai (2.9). Barhte hue function ki sab se chhoti value left end par aur sab se bari right end par hoti hai.

Function \(f\) ka global maximum \(x = 2\) par aur global minimum \(x = 0\) par hai. Values yeh hain:
\[f(2) = 4 \text{ (global maximum value)}\]
\[f(0) = 0 \text{ (global minimum value)}\]
(Figure 2.2 dekhiye.)
Kyun: \(0 \le x \le 2\) ho to \(0 \le x^{2} \le 4\), yani interval ke har \(x\) ke liye \(f(0) \le f(x) \le f(2)\). Yeh bilkul definition wali shart hai.
Tasdeeq: \(f(1) = 1\) aur \(f(1.5) = 2.25\); dono 0 aur 4 ke darmiyan hain, koi bhi 4 se bari ya 0 se chhoti nahin.
blocks.answer: Global maximum value \(f(2) = 4\); global minimum value \(f(0) = 0\).

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: axes with ticks 1 and 2 on the x-axis and 1 to 4 on the y-axis. The curve f(x) = x squared runs from the origin, labelled f(0) = 0, up to the dot (2, 4), labelled f(2) = 4. A dashed red line drops from (2, 4) to the x-axis and a dot marks 4 on the y-axis.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.2: f(x) = x² on [0, 2] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Example (b)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{2}\), poori real line par.
Maloom karna: absolute extrema.
Tareeqa: \(x^{2} \ge 0\) ki madad se \(f(x)\) ka \(f(0)\) se muqabla.

\[f(x) = x^{2} \ge 0 = f(0)\]
Yani \(f\) ki absolute minimum value \(x = 0\) par hai, aur \(f(0) = 0\). (Figure 2.3 dekhiye.)
Kyun: kisi bhi real number ka square negative nahin hota, is liye 0 se neeche koi value nahin.

Is ki koi absolute maximum value nahin.
Kyun: aap koi bhi bara number \(M\) sochiye, \(x = \sqrt{|M|} + 1\) lene se \(x^{2} > M\) ho jata hai. Values bina had ke barhti hain, is liye koi "sab se bari" value nahin.
blocks.answer: Absolute minimum value \(f(0) = 0\); koi absolute maximum nahin.

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: the x-axis marked from minus 2 to 2 and the y-axis from 0 to 3. The upward parabola f(x) = x squared has its lowest point at the dot at the origin, labelled f(0) = 0.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.3: f(x) = x² on (−∞, ∞) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Example (c)
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = -x^{2} + 2\), poori real line par.
Maloom karna: absolute extrema.
Tareeqa: \(-x^{2} \le 0\) ki madad se \(f(x)\) ka \(f(0)\) se muqabla.

\[f(x) = 2 - x^{2} \le 2 = f(0)\]
Yani \(f\) ki absolute maximum value \(x = 0\) par hai, aur \(f(0) = 2\). (Figure 2.4 dekhiye.)
Kyun: 2 mein se hamesha ek non-negative number \(x^{2}\) minus ho raha hai, is liye jawab 2 se bara nahin ho sakta.

Is ki koi absolute minimum value nahin.
Kyun: \(x\) barhta jaye to \(-x^{2} + 2\) har number se neeche chala jata hai (misaal: \(f(10) = -98\), \(f(100) = -9998\)).
blocks.answer: Absolute maximum value \(f(0) = 2\); koi absolute minimum nahin.

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: the x-axis marked from minus 2 to 2 and the y-axis from 0 to 3. The downward parabola f(x) = minus x squared plus 2 has its highest point at the dot (0, 2), labelled f(0) = 2, and crosses the x-axis between 1 and 2 on each side.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.4: f(x) = −x² + 2 on (−∞, ∞) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
(a) aur (b) ka muqabla kijiye: formula ek hi hai, \(x^{2}\), lekin closed interval \([0, 2]\) par global maximum hai aur \((-\infty, \infty)\) par nahin. Farq sirf interval ka hai.
Ek pakka usool yaad rakhiye: closed interval \([a, b]\) par continuous (bina toote) function ka global maximum aur global minimum dono hamesha maujood hote hain (extreme value theorem). Isi liye 2.10.3 ka tareeqa closed interval par kaam karta hai.

rows: Maan lijiye \(I\) ek interval aur \(f: I \to \mathbb{R}\) ek function hai. \(f\) ka \(x = c \in I\) par local (relative) maximum hai, agar koi open interval \(I_{1}\) maujood ho jis mein \(c \in I_{1}\) aur: \(I \cap I_{1}\) ke har \(x\) ke liye \(f(c) \ge f(x)\).

Maan lijiye \(I\) ek interval aur \(f: I \to \mathbb{R}\) ek function hai. \(f\) ka \(x = e \in I\) par local (relative) minimum hai, agar koi open interval \(I_{1}\) maujood ho jis mein \(e \in I_{1}\) aur: \(I \cap I_{1}\) ke har \(x\) ke liye \(f(e) \le f(x)\).
Agar \(f(x)\) ka \(x = c\) par local (relative) maximum ho, to \(f(c)\) function ki local (relative) maximum value kehlati hai. (Figure 2.5)
Agar \(f(x)\) ka \(x = e\) par local (relative) minimum ho, to \(f(e)\) function ki local (relative) minimum value kehlati hai. (Figure 2.5)
blocks.caption: Local (relative) maxima aur minima (kitab ki definitions)

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: an x-axis with the points a, c, e, d, b and a blue curve y = f(x) from a to b, with dashed lines from the curve down to each point. Labels: a, Absolute minimum (no smaller value of f anywhere, also a local minimum); c, Local maximum (no greater value of f nearby); e, Local minimum (no smaller value of f nearby); d, Absolute maximum (no greater value of f anywhere, also a local maximum); b, Local minimum. Short flat lines touch the curve at c and e.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.5: absolute and local extrema of y = f(x) on [a, b] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
Teaching note
blocks.text: Definition mein open interval \(I_{1}\) "aas paas" ka ilaqa hai, aur \(I \cap I_{1}\) us ilaqe ke sirf woh points rakhta hai jo domain mein bhi hon. Isi wajah se end point (jaise \(a\) ya \(b\)) bhi local extremum ho sakta hai: wahan hum sirf ek taraf ke points se muqabla karte hain, kyun ke doosri taraf domain hi khatam ho chuka hai.

rows: Sirf point ke aas paas ke chhote open interval \(I_{1}\) ke \(x\) se muqabla
Zyada se zyada ek maximum value aur ek minimum value
Kai local maxima aur minima ho sakte hain
Mumkin hai maujood hi na ho (Examples (b), (c))
Yeh bhi maujood na ho, mumkin hai (misaal: seedhi line)
Har global extremum local bhi hota hai
Har local extremum global nahin hota (Figure 2.5 mein c aur e)
blocks.caption: Global aur local extrema ka muqabla (hamari taraf se, kitab mein nahin)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(f(x) = x^{3} - 3x\), interval \([-2, 3]\) par. \(f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 3 = 3(x - 1)(x + 1)\), to stationary points \(x = -1\) aur \(x = 1\).
Values: \(f(-2) = -8 + 6 = -2\), \(f(-1) = -1 + 3 = 2\), \(f(1) = 1 - 3 = -2\), \(f(3) = 27 - 9 = 18\).
\(x = -1\) par local maximum (value 2): yeh ek chhoti pahari hai. \(x = 1\) par local minimum (value \(-2\)). Global maximum 18 hai, right end \(x = 3\) par: yani local maximum 2 global se bohat neecha hai.
Dilchasp baat: global minimum value \(-2\) do jagah aati hai, left end \(x = -2\) par bhi aur \(x = 1\) par bhi. Value ek hai, points do. Isi liye definition mein \(\le\) hai, \(<\) nahin.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Jab sawal "global aur local extrema" dono maange (jaise Exercise 2.4 ka Question 4), to har point ke saath do baatein likhiye: woh local hai ya nahin, aur global hai ya nahin. Misaal: "\(x = 3\): local maximum, aur global maximum bhi". End points ko bhi is fehrist mein shamil kijiye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Figure 2.5 mein \(c\) par local maximum hai aur \(b\) par local minimum. Kaunsi value bari hai, \(f(c)\) ya \(f(b)\)? (Jawab: figure mein \(f(b)\) thori kam hai, magar aisa bhi ho sakta tha ke \(b\) wali local minimum value \(c\) wali local maximum value se bhi oonchi ho. Local ka matlab sirf "apne mohalle mein" hai.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(f(x) = \cos x\), interval \([0, \pi]\) par: global maximum aur global minimum kya hain? (Jawab: \(f'(x) = -\sin x \le 0\) is interval mein, yani \(\cos x\) yahan decreasing hai. Is liye sab se bari value left end par \(f(0) = 1\) aur sab se chhoti right end par \(f(\pi) = -1\). Dono extrema end points par hain, andar koi turning point nahin. Ghor kijiye: \(\sin x\) to \(0\) aur \(\pi\) par zero hai, magar woh end points hain, andar ke points nahin.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek aakhri baat definitions ke baare mein: local maximum ki definition mein "koi open interval \(I_{1}\) maujood ho" ka matlab yeh hai ke humein sirf itna dikhana hai ke point ke gird koi na koi chhota sa ilaqa aisa hai jahan woh sab se ooncha hai. Woh ilaqa kitna bhi chhota ho sakta hai. Is liye local maximum dhoondte waqt hum sirf point ke bilkul qareeb dekhte hain: dono taraf graph neeche ho to local maximum, dono taraf ooncha ho to local minimum.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(c\) par global minimum: interval ke har \(x\) ke liye \(f(c) \le f(x)\); global extrema = global maximum aur minimum.
2. \([0, 2]\) par \(x^{2}\): max 4 (\(x = 2\) par), min 0 (\(x = 0\) par); \((-\infty, \infty)\) par: min 0, koi max nahin.
3. \((-\infty, \infty)\) par \(-x^{2} + 2\): max 2 (\(x = 0\) par), koi min nahin.
4. Local extrema sirf qareebi points se muqabla karte hain; end points bhi local extrema ho sakte hain.
5. Har global extremum local bhi hai, magar har local global nahin.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Yeh kehna ke \((-\infty, \infty)\) par \(x^{2}\) ka maximum hai: koi nahin.
2. Kisi chhote ilaqe ki sab se oonchi chotti ko end points se muqabla kiye baghair global maximum keh dena.
3. Yeh bhool jana ke ek local maximum kisi doosri jagah ke local minimum se neecha bhi ho sakta hai.
